latin: Quinti, si tibi vis oculos debere Catullum
english: Quintius, if you want Catullus to owe you his eyes
note: Quinti: vocative of Quintius.

latin: aut aliud si quid carius est oculis,
english: or anything else, if anything is dearer than eyes,

latin: eripere ei noli multo quod carius illi
english: do not snatch from him what much dearer to him

latin: est oculis seu quid carius est oculis.
english: is than eyes, or whatever is dearer than eyes.

latin: Lesbia mi praesente viro mala plurima dicit:
english: Lesbia to me, her husband being present, says very many bad things:
note: mi mala dicit: speaks ill of me, abuses me.

latin: haec illi fatuo maxima laetitia est.
english: this to that fool is the greatest joy.
note: illi fatuo: the husband.

latin: mule, nihil sentis. si nostri oblita taceret,
english: Mule, you perceive nothing. If, forgetful of us, she were silent,
note: mule: vocative, an insult to the husband. nostri: of me (poetic plural).

latin: sana esset: nunc quod gannit et obloquitur,
english: she would be sane: now, because she snarls and rails,
note: gannit: yelps, snarls like a dog.

latin: non solum meminit, sed, quae multo acrior est res,
english: not only does she remember, but, which is a much sharper thing,

latin: irata est: hoc est, uritur et loquitur.
english: she is angry: that is, she burns and speaks.
note: uritur: burns, i.e. with passion.

latin: Chommoda dicebat, si quando commode vellet
english: Chommoda he used to say, if ever commode he wanted
note: Latin forms kept: the joke is Arrius' false aspirate. commoda = 'advantages'; the source prints commode here where most editions read commoda.

latin: dicere, et insidias Arrius hinsidias,
english: to say, and insidias, Arrius, hinsidias,
note: insidias: 'ambush'; dicebat understood from line 1: for insidias Arrius said hinsidias.

latin: et tum mirifice sperabat se esse locutum
english: and then marvellously he hoped himself to have spoken

latin: cum quantum poterat dixerat hinsidias.
english: when as much as he could he had said hinsidias.
note: i.e. with as heavy an aspirate as he could.

latin: credo, sic mater, sic liber avunculus eius,
english: I believe, so his mother, so his free uncle,
note: liber avunculus: 'free(born)' maternal uncle, hinting at a family of freedmen.

latin: sic maternus avus dixerat atque avia
english: so his maternal grandfather had spoken, and grandmother.
note: The source has no punctuation at line end; the sense breaks before line 7.

latin: hoc misso in Syriam requierant omnibus aures:
english: This man sent into Syria, for all, the ears had rested:
note: hoc misso: ablative absolute, 'he having been sent'. omnibus: dative, 'for everyone'.

latin: audibant eadem haec leniter et leviter,
english: they used to hear these same words smoothly and lightly,
note: audibant = audiebant.

latin: nec sibi postilla metuebant talia verba,
english: and did not for themselves thereafter fear such words,

latin: cum subito adfertur nuntius horribilis
english: when suddenly is brought a horrible message

latin: Ionios fluctus, postquam illuc Arrius isset,
english: that the Ionian waves, after Arrius had gone there,

latin: iam non Ionios esse, sed Hionios.
english: now were not Ionios, but Hionios.
note: Latin forms kept: Ionios 'Ionian' with the aspirate added, perhaps punning on Greek chion 'snow'.

latin: Odi et amo. quare id faciam fortasse requiris
english: I hate and I love. Why I do this, perhaps you ask.

latin: nescio, sed fieri sentio et excrucior.
english: I do not know, but I feel it happen and I am crucified.
note: excrucior: 'I am tortured', literally put to the cross (crux).

latin: Quintia formosa est multis, mihi candida, longa,
english: Quintia is beautiful to many; to me, fair, tall,
note: candida: fair-skinned, bright.

latin: recta est. haec ego sic singula confiteor,
english: straight she is. These things I thus one by one admit,

latin: totum illud formosa nego: nam nulla venustas,
english: that whole 'beautiful' I deny: for no charm,
note: totum illud formosa: the whole term formosa, quoted as a word.

latin: nulla in tam magno est corpore mica salis.
english: not one in so great a body is a grain of salt.
note: nulla ... mica salis: salt = wit, piquancy.

latin: Lesbia formosa est, quae cum pulcherrima tota est,
english: Lesbia is beautiful, who, while she is most lovely as a whole,

latin: tum omnibus una omnis subripuit Veneres.
english: then from all women alone has stolen all the Venuses.
note: omnibus: from all (women); Veneres: 'Venuses', i.e. charms, graces.

latin: Nulla potest mulier tantum se dicere amatam
english: No woman can say herself loved so much

latin: vere, quantum a me Lesbia amata mea es
english: truly, as much as by me, Lesbia, mine, you have been loved.
note: Lesbia ... mea: 'my Lesbia'.

latin: nulla fides ullo fuit unquam in foedere tanta
english: No faith in any compact was ever so great
note: foedere: treaty, compact.

latin: quanta in amore tuo ex parte reperta mea est.
english: as in love of you from my part has been found.
note: in amore tuo: in my love for you.

latin: Quid facit is, Gelli, qui cum matre atque sorore
english: What does he do, Gellius, who with mother and sister

latin: prurit et abiectis pervigilat tunicis?
english: itches and, tunics thrown off, stays awake all night?
note: prurit: itches, i.e. is lustful.

latin: quid facit is patruum qui non sinit esse maritum?
english: What does he do who does not allow his uncle to be a husband?
note: patruum: paternal uncle; he cuckolds him with the uncle's wife.

latin: ecquid scis quantum suscipiat sceleris?
english: Do you at all know how much of crime he takes upon himself?

latin: suscipit, o Gelli, quantum non ultima Tethys
english: He takes on, O Gellius, as much as not furthest Tethys
note: ultima Tethys: the sea-goddess at the world's edge, i.e. the remotest sea.

latin: nec genitor nympharum abluit Oceanus:
english: nor the father of the nymphs, Oceanus, washes away:

latin: nam nihil est quicquam sceleris quo prodeat ultra,
english: for there is nothing whatever of crime by which he might go further,

latin: non si demisso se ipse voret capite.
english: not if, his head bent down, he himself should devour himself.
note: i.e. fellate himself.

latin: Gellius est tenuis: quid ni? cui tam bona mater
english: Gellius is thin: why not? he for whom so good a mother

latin: tamque valens vivat tamque venusta soror
english: and so vigorous lives, and so charming a sister,
note: vivat: subjunctive in the relative clause (cui ... vivat).

latin: tamque bonus patruus tamque omnia plena puellis
english: and so good an uncle, and everything so full of girls

latin: cognatis, quare is desinat esse macer?
english: who are kin, why should he cease to be lean?
note: puellis cognatis: girl relatives.

latin: qui ut nihil attingat, nisi quod fas tangere non est,
english: He, even if he touches nothing except what it is not right to touch,
note: qui ut: 'he, even though'. nisi quod fas tangere non est: only what is forbidden to touch.

latin: quantumvis quare sit macer invenies.
english: as much as you like, why he is lean, you will find.

latin: Nascatur magus ex Gelli matrisque nefando
english: Let a magus be born from Gellius' and his mother's unspeakable
note: magus: Persian priest.

latin: coniugio et discat Persicum haruspicium:
english: union, and let him learn Persian soothsaying:
note: haruspicium: haruspicy, divination.

latin: nam magus ex matre et gnato gignatur oportet,
english: for a magus from mother and son must be begotten,

latin: si vera est Persarum impia religio,
english: if true is the impious religion of the Persians,

latin: gratus ut accepto veneretur carmine divos
english: so that, pleasing, with accepted chant he may worship the gods,
note: gratus: welcome (to the gods); accepto carmine: with a chant they accept.

latin: omentum in flamma pingue liquefaciens.
english: melting the fat caul in the flame.
note: omentum: the fatty membrane of the entrails, burnt in sacrifice.

latin: Non ideo, Gelli, sperabam te mihi fidum
english: Not for this reason, Gellius, was I hoping you to me faithful

latin: in misero hoc nostro, hoc perdito amore fore
english: in this wretched love of ours, this ruined love, to be,
note: perdito: lost, ruined, desperate.

latin: quod te cognossem bene constantemve putarem
english: that I had known you well or thought you constant
note: cognossem = cognovissem.

latin: aut posse a turpi mentem inhibere probro,
english: or able from base disgrace to restrain your mind,

latin: sed neque quod matrem nec germanam esse videbam
english: but because neither mother nor sister I saw to be
note: sed neque quod ... nec: but because (she was) neither (your) mother nor (your) sister.

latin: hanc tibi cuius me magnus edebat amor;
english: this woman of yours, a great love of whom was eating me;
note: tibi: dative of relation, 'to you'. edebat: was eating, i.e. consuming.

latin: et quamvis tecum multo coniungerer usu,
english: and although I was joined with you by much intimacy,
note: usu: familiarity, close dealings.

latin: non satis id causae credideram esse tibi.
english: I had not believed that enough of a reason for you.

latin: tu satis id duxti: tantum tibi gaudium in omni
english: You reckoned that enough: so great for you is the joy in every
note: duxti = duxisti.

latin: culpa est in quacumque est aliquid sceleris.
english: fault in which there is anything of crime.

latin: Lesbia mi dicit semper male nec tacet unquam
english: Lesbia to me speaks always ill, nor is she silent ever
note: mi dicit male: speaks ill of me.

latin: de me: Lesbia me dispeream nisi amat.
english: about me: Lesbia, may I perish, unless she loves me.

latin: quo signo? quia sunt totidem mea: deprecor illam
english: By what sign? Because mine are just as many: I curse her
note: totidem mea: the same symptoms are mine. deprecor: I pray against, revile.

latin: adsidue, verum dispeream nisi amo.
english: constantly, but may I perish unless I love.

latin: Nil nimium studeo, Caesar, tibi velle placere,
english: Not at all too much am I eager, Caesar, to want to please you,

latin: nec scire utrum sis albus an ater homo.
english: nor to know whether you are a white or a black man.
note: Proverbial: not to know or care who someone is.

latin: Mentula moechatur. moechatur mentula certe.
english: Mentula commits adultery. Commits adultery a prick, certainly.
note: Mentula: 'Prick', Catullus' nickname for Mamurra; the name kept, the common noun rendered.

latin: hoc est quod dicunt, ipsa olera olla legit.
english: This is what they say: the pot itself picks the greens.
note: Proverb: like seeks like, the pot gathers its own vegetables.

latin: Zmyrna mei Cinnae nonam post denique messem
english: The Zmyrna of my Cinna, after the ninth, at last, harvest
note: Zmyrna: Cinna's epyllion on Myrrha.

latin: quam coepta est nonamque edita post hiemem,
english: from when it was begun, and after the ninth winter, published,
note: post ... quam: after ... (from when).

latin: milia cum interea quingenta Hortensius uno
english: while meanwhile five hundred thousand Hortensius in one

note: Lacuna: a line is lost; usually supplied as 'versiculorum anno putidus evomuit' (verses in one year, rotten, spewed out).

latin: Zmyrna cavas Satrachi penitus mittetur ad undas,
english: Zmyrna will be sent far to the hollow waves of the Satrachus,
note: Satrachus: river in Cyprus, scene of the myth.

latin: Zmyrnam cana diu saecula pervolvent.
english: Zmyrna the grey ages will long unroll.
note: pervolvent: roll through, i.e. read the book-roll.

latin: at Volusi annales Paduam morientur ad ipsam
english: But the annals of Volusius at Padua itself will die

latin: et laxas scombris saepe dabunt tunicas.
english: and loose tunics for mackerel will often give.
note: i.e. become wrapping-paper for fish.

latin: parva mei mihi sint cordi monumenta sodalis:
english: Small, may the monuments of my comrade be dear to me at heart:
note: mihi sint cordi: be at heart to me, i.e. dear.

latin: at populus tumido gaudeat Antimacho.
english: but let the people rejoice in swollen Antimachus.
note: tumido: swollen, bombastic.

latin: Si quicquam mutis gratum acceptumve sepulcris
english: If anything pleasing or welcome to mute tombs

latin: accidere a nostro, Calve, dolore potest,
english: can come from our grief, Calvus,

latin: quo desiderio veteres renovamus amores
english: by which longing we renew old loves
note: quo desiderio: with that longing by which.

latin: atque olim missas flemus amicitias,
english: and weep for friendships once let go,

latin: certe non tanto mors immatura dolori est
english: surely not to so much grief is the untimely death
note: dolori est: predicative dative, 'is a grief'.

latin: Quintiliae, quantum gaudet amore tuo.
english: of Quintilia, as much as she rejoices in your love.
note: Quintilia: Calvus' dead wife (or beloved).

latin: Non (ita me di ament) quicquam referre putavi
english: Not (so may the gods love me) anything did I think it to matter

latin: utrumne os an culum olfacerem Aemilio.
english: whether mouth or arse I should smell of Aemilius.

latin: nilo mundius hoc, nihiloque immundius illud,
english: Not at all cleaner this, and not at all filthier that,
note: hoc: the mouth; illud: the arse.

latin: verum etiam culus mundior et melior:
english: but in fact the arse is cleaner and better:

latin: nam sine dentibus est. hoc dentis sesquipedalis,
english: for it is without teeth. This one teeth a foot and a half long,
note: hoc: the mouth; habet in the next line governs dentis (accusative plural).

latin: gingivas vero ploxeni habet veteris,
english: gums indeed of an old wagon-box it has,
note: ploxeni: ploxenum, a (Gallic) cart-body.

latin: praeterea rictum qualem diffissus in aestu
english: besides a gape such as, split open in the heat,

latin: meientis mulae cunnus habere solet.
english: of a pissing she-mule the cunt is accustomed to have.

latin: hic futuit multas et se facit esse venustum,
english: This man fucks many women and makes himself out to be charming,

latin: et non pistrino traditur atque asino?
english: and is he not handed over to the mill and the ass?
note: pistrino ... asino: the mill-treadmill, a slave's punishment.

latin: quem si qua attingit, non illam posse putemus
english: Whom if any woman touches, would we not think that she could

latin: aegroti culum lingere carnificis?
english: of a sick executioner the arse lick?

latin: In te, si in quemquam, dici pose, putide Victi,
english: Against you, if against anyone, it can be said, putrid Victius,
note: pose: the source's spelling for posse.

latin: id quod verbosis dicitur et fatuis:
english: that which is said of the wordy and the foolish:

latin: ista cum lingua, si usus veniat tibi, possis
english: with that tongue, if occasion should come to you, you could

latin: culos et crepidas lingere carpatinas.
english: arses and peasant brogues lick.
note: crepidas carpatinas: rustic shoes of raw leather.

latin: si nos omnino vis omnes perdere, Victi,
english: If you want to destroy us all entirely, Victius,

latin: hiscas: omnino quod cupis efficies.
english: gape open: entirely what you desire you will accomplish.
note: hiscas: open your mouth, i.e. speak; his breath would kill us.

latin: Subripui tibi, dum ludis, mellite Iuventi,
english: I stole from you, while you were playing, honeyed Iuventius,

latin: saviolum dulci dulcius ambrosia.
english: a little kiss sweeter than sweet ambrosia.

latin: verum id non impune tuli: namque amplius horam
english: But that not unpunished did I carry off: for more than an hour

latin: suffixum in summa me memini esse cruce,
english: fixed on the top of a cross I remember myself to be,
note: Metaphor kept: torment as crucifixion.

latin: dum tibi me purgo nec possum fletibus ullis
english: while I clear myself to you, nor can I with any tears

latin: tantillum vestrae demere saevitiae.
english: take away the tiniest bit of your savagery.
note: vestrae: plural possessive, 'your'.

latin: nam simul id factum est, multis diluta labella
english: For as soon as that was done, the little lips washed with many

latin: guttis abstersisti omnibus articulis,
english: drops you wiped with all your finger-joints,
note: articulis: joints, i.e. fingers.

latin: ne quicquam nostro contractum ex ore maneret,
english: so that nothing contracted from our mouth might remain,

latin: tanquam commictae spurca saliva lupae.
english: as though the foul spittle of a pissed-on she-wolf.
note: lupa: she-wolf, slang for a prostitute; commictae: pissed upon (fouled).

latin: praeterea infesto miserum me tradere Amori
english: Besides, wretched me to hostile Love to hand over

latin: non cessasti omnique excruciare modo,
english: you did not cease, and in every way to torture,

latin: ut mi ex ambrosia mutatum iam fores illud
english: so that for me, changed from ambrosia, now was that
note: fores = esses (archaic subjunctive).

latin: saviolum tristi tristius elleboro.
english: little kiss, more bitter than bitter hellebore.
note: tristis: bitter, harsh (of taste); literally 'sad'.

latin: quam quoniam poenam misero proponis amori,
english: Since this penalty you set out for wretched love,
note: quam quoniam poenam: since which penalty.

latin: nunquam iam posthac basia subripiam.
english: never now hereafter will I steal kisses.

latin: Caelius Aufilenum et Quintius Aufilenam
english: Caelius for Aufilenus and Quintius for Aufilena,
note: Aufilenum, Aufilenam: accusatives, objects of depereunt.

latin: flos Veronensum depereunt iuvenum,
english: the flower of Veronese youths, are perishing utterly,
note: depereunt: perish (with love), i.e. are madly in love with.

latin: hic fratrem, ille sororem. hoc est quod dicitur illud
english: this one the brother, that one the sister. This is what is said, that

latin: fraternum vere dulce sodalicium.
english: brotherly, truly sweet fellowship.
note: Ironic: the two pursuers are like 'brothers' because they love a brother and a sister.

latin: cui faveam potius? Caeli, tibi: nam tua nobis
english: Whom should I favour rather? Caelius, you: for your, to us,

latin: per facta exhibita est unica amicitia
english: through deeds was shown, unique friendship,

latin: cum vesana meas torreret flamma medullas.
english: when the mad flame was scorching my marrow.
note: Metaphor: love as fire in the marrow.

latin: sis felix, Caeli, sis in amore potens.
english: May you be fortunate, Caelius, may you be potent in love.

latin: Multas per gentes et multa per aequora vectus
english: Through many peoples and through many seas carried

latin: advenio has miseras, frater, ad inferias,
english: I arrive at these wretched, brother, funeral offerings,
note: inferias: offerings to the dead.

latin: ut te postremo donarem munere mortis
english: so that I might present you with the last gift of death
note: munere mortis: the gift due to the dead.

latin: et mutam nequiquam adloquerer cinerem,
english: and might address in vain the mute ash,

latin: quandoquidem fortuna mihi tete abstulit ipsum,
english: since fortune has taken from me you yourself,

latin: heu miser indigne frater adempte mihi.
english: alas, wretched brother, unworthily taken from me.

latin: nunc tamen interea haec, prisco quae more parentum
english: Now, however, meanwhile these things, which by the ancient custom of parents
note: parentum: ancestors.

latin: tradita sunt tristi munere ad inferias,
english: have been handed down as a sad gift for funeral offerings,

latin: accipe fraterno multum manantia fletu
english: accept, much streaming with a brother's weeping,
note: fraterno: brotherly.

latin: atque in perpetuum, frater, ave atque vale.
english: and forever, brother, hail and farewell.

latin: Si quicquam tacito commissum est fido ab amico
english: If anything to a silent man has been entrusted by a faithful friend

latin: cuius sit penitus nota fides animi,
english: whose faith of mind is thoroughly known,

latin: meque esse invenies illorum iure sacratum,
english: me too you will find to be consecrated by the law of those men,
note: meque: -que 'and', answering the conditional; illorum: those trusty men.

latin: Corneli, et factum me esse puta Harpocratem.
english: Cornelius, and consider me to have become Harpocrates.
note: Harpocrates: the Egyptian god of silence.

latin: Aut sodes mihi redde decem sestertia, Silo,
english: Either, please, give me back the ten sestertia, Silo,
note: decem sestertia: ten thousand sesterces.

latin: deinde esto quamvis saevus et indomitus:
english: then be as savage and untamed as you like:

latin: aut, si te nummi deIectant, desine quaeso
english: or, if the coins delight you, stop, I ask,
note: deIectant: the source's typography for delectant.

latin: Leno esse atque idem saevus et indomitus.
english: being a pimp and at the same time savage and untamed.

latin: Credis me potuisse meae maledicere vitae,
english: Do you believe that I could have cursed my life,
note: vitae: 'my life', i.e. the beloved.

latin: ambobus mihi quae carior est oculis?
english: who is dearer to me than both eyes?

latin: non potui, nec, si possem, tam perdite amarem:
english: I could not, nor, if I could, would I love so desperately:
note: perdite: ruinously, desperately.

latin: sed tu cum Tappone omnia monstra facis.
english: but you with Tappo make all things monsters.
note: i.e. make monstrous tales out of everything.

latin: Mentula conatur Pipleum scandere montem:
english: Mentula tries to climb the Piplean mountain:
note: Pipleum: of Pimplea, a haunt of the Muses.

latin: Musae furcillis praecipitem eiciunt.
english: the Muses with little pitchforks throw him out headlong.

latin: Cum puero bello praeconem qui videt esse,
english: With a pretty boy whoever sees an auctioneer to be,
note: praeconem: auctioneer, crier.

latin: quid credat, nisi se vendere discupere?
english: what should he believe, except that he longs to sell himself?
note: se: the boy; discupere: to desire greatly.

latin: Si cui quid cupido optantique obtigit unquam
english: If to anyone anything desiring and wishing has fallen ever
note: cupido optantique: dative, to one desiring and wishing.

latin: insperanti, hoc est gratum animo proprie.
english: not hoping, this is welcome to the mind properly.
note: insperanti: dative, to one not hoping.

latin: quare hoc est gratum nobis quoque, carius auro,
english: Therefore this is welcome to us also, dearer than gold,

latin: quod te restituis, Lesbia, mi cupido:
english: that you restore yourself, Lesbia, to me desiring:

latin: restituis cupido atque insperanti, ipsa refers te
english: you restore yourself to one desiring and not hoping, you yourself bring back yourself

latin: nobis. o lucem candidiore nota!
english: to us. O light with a whiter mark!
note: Metaphor: a day to be marked with a white stone, i.e. a lucky day.

latin: quis me uno vivit felicior, aut magis hac res
english: Who lives more fortunate than me alone, or more than this things
note: hac ... vita (next line): ablative of comparison, 'than this life'.

latin: optandas vita dicere quis poterit?
english: to be wished for, life, who will be able to say?

latin: Si, Comini, populi arbitrio tua cana senectus
english: If, Cominius, by the people's judgement your grey old age,

latin: spurcata impuris moribus intereat,
english: befouled by impure ways, should perish,

latin: non equidem dubito quin primum inimica bonorum
english: I do not indeed doubt but that first, hostile to good men,
note: non ... dubito quin: negatives kept as they stand.

latin: lingua exsecta avido sit data vulturio,
english: the tongue cut out would be given to a greedy vulture,

latin: effossos oculos voret atro gutture corvus,
english: the eyes dug out a raven would devour with black gullet,

latin: intestina canes, cetera membra lupi.
english: the intestines the dogs, the other limbs the wolves.

latin: Iucundum, mea vita, mihi proponis amorem
english: Delightful, my life, to me you propose that love
note: mea vita: 'my life', the beloved.

latin: hunc nostrum inter nos perpetuumque fore.
english: this of ours between us and everlasting is to be.

latin: di magni, facite ut vere promittere possit
english: Great gods, make it that truly she can promise

latin: atque id sincere dicat et ex animo,
english: and that she say it sincerely and from the soul,

latin: ut liceat nobis tota perducere vita
english: so that it may be allowed us through all life to carry on

latin: aeternum hoc sanctae foedus amicitiae.
english: this eternal pact of holy friendship.

latin: Aufilena, bonae semper laudantur amicae:
english: Aufilena, good mistresses are always praised:
note: amicae: girlfriends, kept women.

latin: accipiunt pretium quod facere instituunt.
english: they accept the price of what they undertake to do.

latin: tu, quod promisti mihi, quod mentita, inimica es;
english: You, because what you promised me, because you lied, are hostile;
note: promisti = promisisti; mentita (es): you lied.

latin: quod nec das et fers saepe, facts facinus.
english: because you neither give and often take, you do a crime.
note: facts: the source's misprint for facis. nec das et fers: you do not give and yet you take.

latin: aut facere ingenuae est, aut non promisse pudicae,
english: Either to do it is of a free-born woman, or not to have promised of a chaste woman,
note: promisse = promisisse.

latin: Aufilena, fuit: sed data corripere
english: Aufilena, it was: but what is given to snatch

latin: fraudando † efficit plus quam meretricis avarae,
english: by cheating † does more than of a greedy whore,
note: Text corrupt (crux kept); efficit is unsure, emended e.g. to officiis. The sense: worse than a greedy whore.

latin: quae sese toto corpore prostituit.
english: who prostitutes herself with her whole body.

latin: Aufilena, viro contentam vivere solo
english: Aufilena, to live content with one husband alone

latin: nuptarum laus e laudibus eximiis:
english: of brides is the praise from among outstanding praises:

latin: sed cuivis quamvis potius succumbere par est
english: but to lie under anyone whatever, rather, is fitting
note: cuivis quamvis: any woman with any man whatever.

latin: quam matrem fratres ex patruo parere.
english: than as mother to bear brothers from an uncle.
note: fratres ex patruo: children by her uncle, who are her sons and cousins at once.

latin: Multus homo est, Naso, neque tecum multus homo est qui
english: Much of a man he is, Naso, and not with you much of a man is he who
note: multus homo: 'much of a man', a pun on many-sided/great man; the sense of the couplet is obscure.

latin: descendit: Naso, multus es et pathicus.
english: goes down: Naso, you are much, and a pathic.
note: descendit: goes down (to the forum, or in a sexual sense). pathicus: the passive partner in anal sex.

latin: Consule Pompeio primum duo, Cinna, solebant
english: With Pompey consul the first time, two, Cinna, used to have
note: Verb not expressed in the Latin; 'have' supplied from the sexual sense. solebant: 'used to'.

latin: Maeciliam: facto consule nunc iterum
english: Maecilia: now, with him made consul again,

latin: manserunt duo, sed creverunt milia in unum
english: the two have remained, but there have grown thousands for one

latin: singula. fecundum semen adulterio.
english: each. Fertile seed in adultery.
note: singula: each (lover) has become thousands.

latin: Firmanus saltu non falso Mentula dives
english: Firmanian, with his estate, not falsely, Mentula rich
note: Firmanus saltu: by his estate at Firmum.

latin: fertur, qui tot res in se habet egregias,
english: is said to be, who has in it so many outstanding things,
note: in se: in itself (the estate).

latin: aucupium omne genus, piscis, prata, arva, ferasque.
english: fowling of every kind, fish, meadows, ploughland, and wild beasts.

latin: nequiquam: fructus sumptibus exsuperat.
english: In vain: the yield with his expenses he exceeds.

latin: quare concedo sit dives, dum omnia desint;
english: Therefore I grant he is rich, provided all things are lacking;

latin: saltum laudemus, dum domo ipse egeat.
english: let us praise the estate, provided he himself is in need at home.

latin: Mentula habet iuxta triginta iugera prati,
english: Mentula has nearly thirty jugera of meadow,
note: iuxta: nearly; iugera: acres (iugera).

latin: quadraginta arvi: cetera sunt maria.
english: forty of ploughland: the rest are seas.

latin: cur non divitiis Croesum superare potis sit
english: Why not in riches Croesus could he surpass,

latin: uno qui in saltu tot bona possideat,
english: he who in one estate possesses so many goods,

latin: prata, arva, ingentis silvas saltusque paludesque
english: meadows, ploughlands, huge woods and woodland-pastures and marshes

latin: usque ad Hyperboreos et mare ad Oceanum?
english: as far as the Hyperboreans and the sea to Ocean?

latin: omnia magna haec sunt, tamen ipse est maximus ultro,
english: All these are great, yet he himself is greatest beyond them,

latin: non homo, sed vero mentula magna minax.
english: not a man, but truly a prick, great, threatening.
note: mentula: 'prick', pun on the nickname Mentula.

latin: Saepe tibi studioso animo venante requirens
english: Often for you, with a studious mind hunting, seeking
note: animo venante: ablative, with the mind hunting.

latin: carmina uti possem mittere Battiadae
english: how I might be able to send songs of Battiades
note: Battiadae: Callimachus, son of Battus.

latin: qui te lenirem nobis, neu conarere
english: by which I might soften you to us, and that you would not try

latin: tela infesta mihi mittere in usque caput,
english: hostile weapons to send at me even up to my head,
note: Metaphor kept: weapons = abusive verses.

latin: hunc video mihi nunc frustra sumptum esse laborem,
english: this I see now for me in vain has been undertaken, labour,

latin: Gelli, nec nostras hic valuisse preces.
english: Gellius, and our prayers here not to have prevailed.

latin: contra nos tela ista tua evitamus amictu:
english: Against them, those weapons of yours we avoid with a cloak:
note: contra: in turn; amictu: cloak, wrapped garment.

latin: at fixus nostris tu dabis supplicium.
english: but pierced by ours you will pay the penalty.
note: nostris: by our (weapons).
